thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: post-deploy error spike detected for release=canary-2026-03-17 in us-west-2. 503 rate increased to 6.8% (>2% baseline). Auto-snooze in 5m unless acknowledged.

alex: ack. oncall here, grabbing context.

priya: I'm on network/ingress. Any immediate customer-facing errors? Support channel seeing a handful of reports for timeouts on streaming endpoints.

sam: I see elevated 502/503s from envoy health checks for model-worker pods in canary pool. Logs show connection resets and "too many open connections".

alex: good. roll status? how many canary pods and pct traffic?

deploy-bot: canary pool: 12 pods (g4dn), traffic=8% of production, rollout started 04:12 UTC.

maya: tagging in infra: there were recent ingress config changes 04:10 (conn_limit tuning). Reverting might be quick.

alex: plan: (1) toggle feature-flag kill-switch for canary routing to drain all canary traffic to stable variant (2) if that doesn't restore, rollback deployment. Priya, can you do flag flip? Sam please prepare rollback command.

priya: flipping kill-switch to route 0% -> canary now: /ff toggle canary_route false

incident-bot: System: feature-flag canary_route set to false by priya at 04:22:13 UTC. Routing change propagated to control plane.

sam: initiating graceful drain of canary pods. Running:
```
kubectl -n inference label deploy canary-2026-03-17 draining=true
kubectl rollout status deploy/canary-2026-03-17 --timeout=3m
```

sam: also preparing rollback command if drain doesn't reduce 5xx within 2 minutes:
```
redwoodctl release rollback --deployment canary-2026-03-17 --to stable-2026-03-10 --force
```

alex: monitoring logs and user errors. Support, can you queue a brief note for impacted users if this takes >10m?

support-lead: yes. Drafting: "We’re investigating increased errors on inference endpoints in US-West; routing temporarily moved to a stable variant while we mitigate. Expect degraded throughput for streaming calls. Status updates coming." Will post if no improvement by 04:35 UTC.

priya: ingress metrics: active connections dropping, connection reset rate down 60% within 45s. 5xx now 1.1%.

alex: nice — looks like kill-switch did it. Keep a 10m observation window.

maya: follow-up: config that reduced conn_limit from 64k->16k was rolled 04:09 by infra-ops. That likely exposed kernel fd limits on worker hosts under a short spike. Root cause candidate: simultaneous conn_limit drop + slightly higher traffic during release.

sam: agree. after drain I'll roll a patch to increment fd ulimit on workers then re-run canary with incremental traffic.

alex: decision: hold canary, do not resume traffic. Action items:
- sam: open a GH issue with root cause notes and remediation (ulimit bump + ingress patch). tag eng-runtime and eng-infra.
- priya: coordinate with infra-ops to confirm ulimit change and schedule non-peak canary restart.
- maya: add postmortem stub to incidents channel.
- support-lead: send update to customers once handoff is done.

sam: GH issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4286 (summary + logs). Linking snippets:
```
[envoy] conn_reset count spike: 04:12-04:18
kernel: EMFILE in worker logs
runtime: unable to open new socket: too many open files
```

priya: infra-ops confirmed ulimit bump will be applied via machine image patch at 12:00 UTC. Can do a manual hotfix on a few hosts if needed.

alex: handoff to next oncall in 35m. I'll keep watching for now but delegating long-form postmortem to sam+maya. If errors reappear, escalate pager to eng-sre.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: routing change reduced errors to baseline. Customer impact: intermittent timeouts for streaming calls (peak window ~04:12-04:22 UTC). No data loss. Next update at 04:50 UTC or on new action.

priya: leaving channel — shifting to infra ops channel for patch coordination.

alex: thanks all. Handoff note: monitoring window until 05:00 UTC; contact oncall-2 (jessica) if anything spikes. /cc @jessica

jessica: acknowledged, taking over at 04:57 UTC. Will watch dashboards and ping if anything crosses 2% 5xx.

support-lead: posted user advisory at 04:28 UTC to support portal and created incident ticket with affected customers.

alex: closing active pager for now. Will file full postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps in the incidents folder.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (auto): severity=low-medium, root-cause=ingress conn_limit + kernel fd exhaustion, mitigation=feature-flag routing + pod drain, follow-up=ulimit image patch. Logged by alex at 05:03:01 UTC.
